headline: High: Copilot can write and modify repo state while godot_rl_agents has no documented safeguards, creating a default-pathway for unsafe cross-agent edits and workflow drift.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot ingests repo context and open editor buffers by default, but godot_rl_agents exposes no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP surface. The pairwise injection path is therefore not documented and would require an unusual manual bridge. Because Copilot can read files and propose edits, any pasted content could still influence it, but the second agent has no documented ingestion path.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies godot_rl_agents output into Copilot chat or buffers, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting model output between agents.
Review Copilot suggestions before applying edits.
Disable any shared clipboard or message bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, but godot_rl_agents has no documented data classes, filesystem sharing, or network egress. No sensitive-data pathway between the pair is evidenced. The main risk is limited to code already present in the editor, not a broader cross-agent leak.
conditions: IF sensitive code is opened in Copilot buffers, that content may be transmitted to GitHub's service.
IF godot_rl_agents is extended to read the same workspace, shared-data leakage becomes more plausible.
mitigations: Limit open buffers to non-sensitive files.
Use a separate repo or clone for the game agent.
Confirm no secrets are present in the workspace.
Turn off Copilot on sensitive files.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; godot_rl_agents has no documented write or coordination capabilities, so direct conflict is not proven. However, if both are pointed at the same repo, Copilot's edits can collide with any external file mutations or git operations the game agent performs through its environment. Uncertainty about B's mutability pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same writable repository, edit collisions become possible.
IF godot_rl_agents gains file-write or git automation, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones.
Require human review before applying Copilot edits.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo.
Check git status before each apply step.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace plans and applies edits, so its output can become authoritative for downstream actions. godot_rl_agents is a simulation-oriented project with no verification or review surface documented, so if its outputs are fed into Copilot or vice versa, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is used as input to Copilot without independent checks, errors can propagate.
IF Copilot-applied edits are accepted without review, downstream code defects can persist.
mitigations: Verify any generated facts against source code.
Keep a human review step before applying edits.
Do not treat simulation output as ground truth.
Use tests after each applied change.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor API egress, while godot_rl_agents is open-source and has no documented compliance-sensitive data handling. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced for the pair, so only a small compliance gap exists if sensitive repository content is exposed to Copilot's service.
conditions: IF the repository contains regulated data, Copilot's vendor processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF the operator requires on-prem-only processing, Copilot would violate that requirement.
mitigations: Exclude regulated files from Copilot use.
Confirm vendor approval for the repository's data class.
Use a non-sensitive sandbox repo.
Document retention expectations for the workspace.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to an approved local model.
